newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir says Perwaja rescue to cost $400 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir says Perwaja rescue to cost $400 mln.

text.p: Rescuers of Malaysia's Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd need to invest more than a billion ringgit ($400 million) to revive the ailing national steel company, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday.
"If we have the confidence, I feel we can revive this plant," Mahathir was quoted as saying by the national Bernama news agency after a visit to the plant in eastern Terengganu state.
"We cannot but stress the importance of a steel industry as a yardstick of the developed status of a country," he said.

Perwaja, a 10-year-old pet project of Mahathir, was found earlier this year to have accumulated losses of 2.9 billion ringgit and its previous government-appointed managers were accused of financial mismanagement.

Perwaja was then entrusted to relatively-unknown Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd and the Lion Group to rescue the company. But Lion backed out after it expressed displeasure with the 30 percent stake offered to it, as compared to Maju's 51 percent.
Mahathir said his government was still working out Perwaja's privatisation plan, adding that Equal Concept Sdn Bhd, a Maju-led company, would manage Perwaja in the interim period.
He said Perwaja was originally launched as a government project because steel was a difficult industry and too risky for the private sector to start a business in.
But now, the government had decided to privatise Perwaja to give its managers more responsibility over the firm's assets, he said.
"The private sector has to invest its own money... and if there are losses, it must incur its own losses," Mahathir said.
He said it was imperative that Perwaja be successful as the project reflected the capability of the country's indigenous Malays, or Bumiputra, and his government wanted to recoup the money invested.
"Perwaja was my idea, if it fails, I will be embarrassed," he said.
